name: ACR Stealer
loaders: unknown (not yet characterized in public reporting)
distribution_channels: Russian forums (observed in XSS marketplace listings)
notes: Newly discovered family. Info.txt is YAML-shaped (not INI, not plain keyvalue), which is unusual in this ecosystem and was the hinge that led us to add YAML support to the rule engine. Observed in Khazan intake with ~57 folders carrying the YAML Info.txt. Dead-drop resolver (DDR) technique for C2 fetch. No rules in our catalog yet; add when we see enough samples to characterize the output shape stably across builds.

name: AnyDesk remote-desktop client
distribution_channels: targeted by ransomware operators pre-encryption (initial-access reuse)
notes:
AnyDesk stores its client state in three keyvalue files under %APPDATA%/AnyDesk (or %PROGRAMDATA%/AnyDesk for service-mode):

  service.conf   installed-service state. Carries 'ad.anynet.pkey'
                 (the device's RSA PRIVATE KEY, PEM with literal
                 \n line escapes), 'ad.license.state_store' (the
                 license binding), and the anynet client stats hash.
  system.conf    machine-wide settings. Holds 'ad.anynet.id' (the
                 stable AnyDesk ID, e.g. 1319043527), 'ad.license.name',
                 'ad.anynet.alias', 'ad.anynet.network_id'.
  user.conf      per-user UI + invitation / roster state.

The AnyDesk ID + the device private key together = silent device takeover: an attacker can impersonate the victim's AnyDesk device on the AnyDesk network without ever needing the unattended-access password. This is one of the highest-value credential targets in a stealer log and one that every popular stealer (Lumma, StealC v2, RedLine, Acreed, Opus) grabs by default.
Observed in the Khazan sample as the trio of service/system/user.conf siblings under Software/AnyDsk/ (vowel-stripped).

name: Browser autofill entries
notes:
Browser form-autofill entries: Name = form field name, Value = user input. Captures everything an operator can later use to impersonate the victim at signup / KYC / shipping: CPF, CEP, DataNascimento, phone numbers, addresses, credit card holder names, shipping names.
Dominant shape in Khazan intake:
  Name: <field>
  Value: <input>
  ===============

Opus WEB RAT writes the same data under Browsers/AtFs/<browser>_<profile>.txt with the vowel-stripped 'AtFs' dir name. StealC v1 writes under Autofill/ with Title-case 'Chrome_<Profile>.txt' filenames.

name: Browser bookmarks
notes:
Flat URL list, one bookmark per line. No title / folder metadata (the stealer flattens Chrome's bookmarks.json structure to just the URLs). Useful signal for operator interest-profiling: which banks, which crypto exchanges, which internal corp URLs, which admin panels the victim had saved.
Opus writes Browsers/Bmas/<browser>_<profile>.txt (vowel-stripped). Older stealers write under Bookmarks/ with Title-case filenames.

name: Browser-saved passwords
notes:
Meta-family for the plain-text password dumps every stealer ships. Three distinct block shapes seen in Khazan intake:

  A. Title-case + blank-line separator: Soft / Host / Login / Password
     (402 of 439 victims; StealC v1, Lumma, Opus, most others)
  B. UPPERCASE + blank-line separator: SOFT / URL / USER / PASS
     (37 victims; json_v2 cluster = StealC v2 / Acreed / Stealerium)
  C. Title-case + '===============' divider: URL / Username / Password
     (RedLine Passwords.txt)

Variants A + B may include android://hash@pkg/ URLs in the host slot when the credential came from a mobile app login. All three shapes may contain empty Login / USER values and empty Password / PASS values (stealer captured the record anyway).

name: Combolist (non-stealer drop)

references.title: Have I Been Pwned combolist methodology

notes: Meta-family, not a stealer. Flat url:user:pass (or ;/|-separated) files that aggregate credentials from many sources and campaigns. Our combolist_container rule fires as the L1 fallback when no stealer family matches; the per-shape probes (combolist_ulp_colon, _semicolon, _pipe, _any_scheme, _schemeless, _email_colon, _android, _ulpextract_tsv) classify the row format. ulpextract remains the authoritative per-row credential ingester.

name: Browser cookies (Netscape format)
distribution_channels: inside stealer-log drops (every family exports browser cookies)
standalone cookie dumps on forum marketplaces
notes: Meta-family for the de-facto cookie.txt format. Tab-separated with seven columns: domain, include_subdomains, path, secure, expires, name, value. Lines starting with # are comments and blank lines are skipped. Every stealer family ships cookies in this format somewhere under Browsers/ or Cookies/; our Netscape probe rule classifies the file shape regardless of which stealer produced it.

name: FileZilla FTP client saved sites
notes:
FileZilla is the single most common Windows FTP client. sitemanager.xml is the operator's saved-sites list; recentservers.xml is the recent- connection list. Both carry per-server Host / Port / Protocol / User / Pass. Pass is base64-encoded (NOT encrypted; obfuscation only) with the 'encoding="base64"' attribute on the <Pass> element; plaintext recovery is one b64decode call.
High-value shape for CTI pivoting: operators often save personal NAS, corp staging servers, shared hosting control panels, and legacy FTP endpoints here. Compromise of one FileZilla export regularly yields dozens of unique credential sets.

name: Gabb file-grabber (sidecar)
distribution_channels: sidecar module inside json_v2 drops (StealC v2 / Acreed / Stealerium)
notes:
Sidecar FILE-GRABBER module shipped inside json_v2 drops (seen alongside pc_info.json + log_info.json + passwords.tsv). Walks the Windows user profile and buckets grabbed files into vowel-stripped directories.
Top-level profile buckets observed:
  Dstp = Desktop
  Dmts = Documents
  Dwas = Downloads
  Rt   = (undetermined; CVs + text files + TV-series notes seen,
          possibly Recent or a catch-all)

Nested type buckets (inside each profile dir):
  Cmpss   = Compressed (.zip / .rar / .7z)
  Pgams   = Programs (installers, scripts)
  V       = Videos
  Ptabs   = Portables (portable apps, filenames carry .P / .Ptab suffix)
  Fma Eta = Firma Electrónica (p12 certs; Spanish-locale giveaway)
  hha     = banking docs (seen with 'DATOS BANCARIOS.docx')

Filenames inside buckets are also vowel-stripped as light obfuscation. Zero public reporting as of 2026-11; name coined from the folder. Expand this family entry as more variants surface.

name: JSON-first cluster (StealC v2 / Acreed / Stealerium)
notes: Synthetic family in our catalog: we lump StealC v2 / Acreed / Stealerium because single-folder disambiguation is not reliable without BuildID prefix inspection or C2 telemetry. Sub-tagging rule keyed off log_info.BuildID is a follow-up. All three emit the same pc_info.json + log_info.json + passwords.tsv surface.

name: Lumma Stealer
notes: Native builds start with a "Lumma Stealer Report" banner; repackers (Khazan et al.) overwrite the banner with their channel ads. HWID is UUID-style (vs Raccoon's 32-hex). DOJ + Microsoft takedown May 2025; infrastructure substantially rebuilt by Q3 2025, treat as active. Native info file shape is "- Key: Value" dash prefix.

name: Meta Stealer

references.title: Europol Operation Magnus (Oct 2024, RedLine + Meta takedown)

notes: Direct RedLine fork that reused most of the UserInformation.txt surface. Taken down alongside RedLine in Operation Magnus (Oct 2024). Log dumps from early 2024 and prior still circulate; new infections effectively zero. Our redline_container rule will also match Meta samples by filename; a disambiguating rule off the actor-handle string inside UserInformation.txt is a possible follow-up.

name: Mystic Stealer
notes: Django-based control panel (unusual; most crimeware panels are PHP). Output surface overlaps StealC and Vidar (information.txt filename); Mystic's distinguisher is the C2 handshake protocol, not the on-disk files. Our catalog has no Mystic-specific rule; samples that hit our stealc_container but fail the StealC [Hardware] INI probe fall back to the generic combolist handling.

name: Opus (WEB RAT)
distribution_channels: private operator panel (/api/logs/download serves per-HWID zips)
notes: Rust stub ("Opus"). Per-HWID zip layout served from the operator panel at /api/logs/download. Distinctive: ships UserInformation.txt (filename clash with RedLine) BUT has worklog.txt, Clients/MAX.txt (ru MAX messenger), and Telegram/ with tdata + AyuGram / Kotatogram / Telegram UWP forks, which no other family emits together. FileGrabber output in Files/ is operator-configurable via the panel's `logcollector`. Wallet coverage is chromium extensions (Phantom, Binance, Bitapp, BoltX, ...) plus on-disk %LOCALAPPDATA% wallet dirs zipped under Wallets/. Operator has API docs + an account; a dedicated dossier rule can extract system/user recon from UserInformation.txt safely because the Opus container rule disambiguates vs RedLine first.

name: Raccoon Stealer
notes: v1 died with the 2022 arrest of the primary operator. v2 (sometimes called RecordBreaker) appeared mid-2022 and continued through 2024. Both v1 and v2 ship System.txt and collide with Lumma on filename; tiebreak is HWID shape (Raccoon: 32-hex; Lumma: UUID-style) and the per-browser-profile directory layout (Raccoon writes Browsers/<Browser>/<Profile>_pws.txt, Lumma writes Chrome/<Profile>/Passwords.txt).

name: RedLine Stealer

references.title: Europol Operation Magnus (Oct 2024, RedLine + Meta takedown)

notes: Operation Magnus (Oct 2024) seized core infrastructure. Still appears in log dumps through 2026 but net new infections dropped sharply. Fingerprint keys: Uptime, Keyboards, Language with [0xNNNN] LCID. Per-browser passwords live in Browsers/<Browser>/Passwords.txt (capital P), the most specific signature.

name: Rhadamanthys
notes: Multi-component architecture with modular grabber plugins. Known for aggressive crypto-wallet and messenger coverage. No rules shipped in our catalog yet; Rhadamanthys samples rare in our Khazan intake (Khazan is mostly a stealer-RESELLER channel, not a Rhadamanthys licensing channel). Add rules when a Rhadamanthys-first source appears.

name: StealC (v1)

references.title: SentinelOne, StealC a copycat of Vidar and Raccoon

notes: Original v1 line continues alongside the unrelated v2 rewrite (which is JSON-first and ships as the json_v2 cluster in our catalog). information.txt has a plain "Key: Value" header BLOCK followed by [Hardware] and [Software] INI sections. [Software] is a bare program list, no `=` separator.

name: Steam saved accounts
distribution_channels: inside any stealer that grabs the Steam config dir
notes: loginusers.vdf lives at Steam/config/loginusers.vdf on Windows (or in the vowel-stripped Software/Stam/ sidecar that json_v2 stealers emit). Lists every account that has touched this Steam install, keyed by SteamID64 (76561198*), with AccountName + PersonaName + Timestamp + AutoLogin + RememberPassword flags. The RememberPassword flag paired with a captured ssfn* session file = session-takeover without the account password.

name: Vidar Stealer
notes: Forked from Arkei, which in turn forked from an earlier commodity codebase. StealC is a Vidar clone and reuses the same output surface (information.txt). In practice, repackers normalize these so hard that single-folder disambiguation fails; our stealc_container rule tags them stealc_or_vidar when the banner dominates and leaves Vidar-specific disambiguation to a wallet-dir probe (not yet built). Vidar 10.x shipped 2025; 2026 builds in wild.

name: Windows credential manager export
distribution_channels: inside stealer-log drops (anything that calls CredEnumerate + DPAPI unwrap)
notes:
Export of the victim's Windows Credential Manager (DPAPI-unwrapped). Covers: domain credentials, Microsoft account tokens, OneDrive refresh tokens, Xbox Live auth (seen with 'Target: MCLMS|...' + base64 JWT in the Pass field), stored credentials for mapped network drives, mstsc RDP saved creds, Outlook / Thunderbird SMTP passwords, and anything a victim app wrote via CredWrite().
Dominant shape:
  Target: <credential-target-name>
  User: <username or N/A>
  Pass: <base64 blob OR plaintext password>
  <blank line>

High-value evidence; the Pass field often holds long base64/JWT tokens and passwords should be treated as plaintext even when they look like garbage (they frequently are OAuth refresh tokens).
